summary.text: A 76-year-old Caucasian woman developed urticaria pigmentosa in 2014 and was diagnosed with indolent systemic mastocytosis (increased tryptase, splenomegaly, osteoporosis, cKIT D816V) and treated with anti-H1/H2, antiresorptive and anti-mediator therapy, with spleen resizing and clinical improvement for nearly a decade.

In March 2023 she presented again with cutaneous, constitutional and gastrointestinal symptoms; restaging showed tryptase 281 microg/L, moderate anemia, lymphocytosis, organomegalies, neoplastic mast cells (20%) and monoclonal B cells (50%) with del(13q14), del(17p13), TP53 mutation and unmutated IGHV, leading to smoldering SM with high-risk CLL.

In March 2024 CLL progressed with severe anemia and lymphocytosis 44x10^(9)/L and thrombocytopenia (platelets 48x10^(9)/L); avapritinib was avoided and acalabrutinib monotherapy was started at 100 mg/die, then 200 mg one month later; midostaurin was declined by the patient.

She became transfusion independent after four months, CLL reached partial remission by February 2025, tryptase fell from 155 to 45.6 microg/L within six months, SM-related manifestations resolved and SM was considered in partial remission; at October 2025 follow-up tryptase was 36.5 microg/L, KIT D816V was no longer detected on peripheral blood NGS and a bone marrow reassessment was declined.
